front.title: Enterprise Deployment Considerations for Post-Quantum TLS Server Authentication in the Public Web PKI

author.organization: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan

abstract.t:
The migration of TLS server authentication to post-quantum mechanisms in the public Web PKI must fit the scale and complexity of enterprise certificate management and TLS termination. Public-facing services may support tens of millions of customers using unmanaged browsers, mobile applications, and other TLS clients, while authentication infrastructure is distributed across business units, hosting providers, cloud platforms, and CDNs. Deployment readiness therefore depends on cryptographic and protocol support as well as the ability to introduce new authentication mechanisms without disrupting customer access.
This document examines enterprise deployment considerations for standalone Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs) and conventional standalone ML-DSA certificates on public websites accessed by unmanaged clients. It addresses certificate issuance, provisioning, renewal, revocation, trust-anchor signaling, credential selection, and interoperability across browsers, certificate-management systems, and TLS termination platforms.
Drawing on initial browser and TLS client observations, the document identifies deployment dependencies, proposes interoperability questions for implementers, and discusses migration priorities and operational readiness. It does not define new certificate formats or TLS mechanisms, assume that either certificate approach is easier to deploy, or commit the authors to independently testing supplier implementations.
